target_customer: Hospitals and urologists performing endourology procedures, starting with HoLEP prostate enucleation
problem: Surgical robots help with the physical side of surgery but not the cognitive side; surgery remains hard to learn and outcomes vary by surgeon.
business_model: Medical device capital equipment and procedure-linked sales (details not found)
product_category: Autonomous surgical robotics and surgical AI

founders.name: Nick Damiano
previous_startups: Avail MedSystems (formerly Nurep, since acquired by Mendaera)
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page. Venture partner at Pioneer Fund.

founders.name: Kartik Tiwari
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page he led the team at Starsky Robotics and is a technical founder of three companies, two YC-backed. Education not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous surgical robot with AI anatomy mapping, hardware and regulatory clearance for a clinical procedure; the YC page says the first robot was built in about three months and is hardware-lite.

defensibility.rationale: Clinical trial data, device clearance and surgical data collection raise barriers; partnerships with Richard Wolf and Quanta System support the stack.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action against Andromeda found in sources. Incumbents are named from general context and not confirmed by a dated source.

market_need_then: The company states robots perform about a quarter of surgeries but only help physically, and prostate enlargement is a large urology procedure. Demand evidence beyond the company's own framing was not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Ambitious, with claims like the Tesla of Surgical Robotics and calling the software a sous surgeon; the site notes information reflects design goals

branding.community_and_virality: A podcast episode titled The Tesla of Surgical Robotics exists; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive name and clear positioning phrases, with press for the first robotic HoLEP in December 2024, but little brand coverage as such.

outcome_analysis: Andromeda is active. It performed what it calls the first robotic assisted HoLEP in Chile in December 2024, started the ASTRA trial, signed partnerships with Richard Wolf and Quanta System in 2025, and reported a $15M Series A led by Standard Capital in August 2026. Repeat founders with medtech and autonomy experience and clinical progress explain the raise, while commercialization and regulatory risk remain.
notes: Series A label comes from Vestbee, Dealroom and aggregator summaries; Runtimewire does not state the stage. Reports of total funding around $30M and a $500K earlier seed or pre-seed on aggregators are unverified and not recorded as rounds. A Caplight headline about a $16M round led by BlackRock appears to be unrelated site text. No competitor sources dated near the 2023 batch were found, so the list is empty. The one-liner for Series A investors varies by source.
